classes.name: Élections de la Chambre des représentants / Verkiezingen voor de Kamer van volksvertegenwoordigers
classes.note: Directly elected by list proportional representation in electoral districts: arrondissements until 1991, 20 constituencies in 1995 and 1999, and 11 provincial constituencies from 2003 (with Brussels-Halle-Vilvoorde until 2012). 150 members since 1995 (Art. 63), 212 from 1949 to 1991. Before 1919 the Chamber was renewed by halves of the provinces every two years, save after a dissolution. Belgium holds no by-elections: a vacancy goes to the next substitute on the list. Seats are divided by D'Hondt within each constituency (Code électoral Art. 167); each province and Brussels-Capital is a constituency (Art. 87). Voting has been compulsory since 1893 (Art. 62).

cadence.locator: https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/cgi_loi/change_lg.pl?language=fr&la=F&cn=1994021730&table_name=loi (Art. 65: "Les membres de la Chambre des représentants sont élus pour cinq ans. La Chambre est renouvelée intégralement tous les cinq ans. Les élections pour la Chambre ont lieu le même jour que les élections pour le Parlement européen.")

cadence.vacancy_rule: No by-election: the first substitute (suppléant / opvolger) of the member's list takes the seat.

classes.name: Élections communales / Gemeenteraadsverkiezingen / Gemeinderatswahlen
classes.note: Every municipal council is elected by list PR, with Imperiali divisors (1, 1.5, 2, ...) in all three regions (LPKD Art. 166; CDLD L4145-5; Brussels), every six years on the second Sunday of October (Flanders: Lokaal en Provinciaal Kiesdecreet Art. 6; Wallonia: CDLD; Brussels: Brussels electoral ordinance). Organized by the federal Interior until 2000 and by the regions (and for its nine municipalities the German-speaking Community from 2018) since 2006. Flanders ended compulsory voting for local elections in 2024. Mayors are not elected separately (mayor class). The federal service publishes municipal results only for 1976 to 2000; the regions publish from 2006.

classes.name: Bourgmestre / Burgemeester
classes.disposition_reason: No separate vote: in Wallonia (CDLD L1123-4) and since 2024 in Flanders the councillor with the most preference votes on the largest majority list becomes mayor, and in Brussels the regional government appoints one of the councillors (Nouvelle loi communale Art. 13); the council election already holds those votes.

classes.locator: https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/cgi_loi/change_lg.pl?language=fr&la=F&cn=1994021730&table_name=loi (Art. 41, last paragraph: matters of municipal or provincial interest may be the subject of a popular consultation)
classes.disposition_reason: Non-binding consultations called by individual municipalities and provinces since the law of 10 April 1995; no regional or federal register lists them or their results, so each must be found in its own municipality's records.

classes.name: Consultation populaire régionale
classes.note: Art. 39bis lets the regions hold consultations on their exclusive matters; none has been held.
